perspective:
Maria knows she and Cheryl are colleagues at the community center, have worked together occasionally, and have a professional relationship that has been growing into a personal friendship, including conversations about their cultural backgrounds and life experiences.

She observed Cheryl looking stressed and overwhelmed by paperwork and planning for the outreach project, so she offered help. Cheryl accepted, saying she could definitely use it. Maria then helped Cheryl with the project and noticed Cheryl handling responsibilities better and showing more confidence.

At a staff meeting, Maria suggested Cheryl lead the next phase, saying Cheryl had shown great aptitude and commitment. She heard the team leader call it a good suggestion and ask Cheryl if she wanted the role. Cheryl thanked Maria and said she was ready to take on the challenge.

Later, Maria privately approached Cheryl because she worried Cheryl might feel pressured or that Maria had overstepped. She told Cheryl she wanted her to feel supported, not pressured. Cheryl said she had been a bit surprised but appreciated Maria’s support and that Maria’s belief in her meant a lot.

After that, Maria felt relieved Cheryl valued her honesty and support. She proposed they co-lead the project together. Cheryl agreed, saying it was a fantastic idea, that Maria’s guidance had been invaluable, and that they made a great team.

After several successful collaborations, Maria felt joyful about their partnership and suggested teaming up for future projects. Cheryl said she would love that, called working with Maria a wonderful experience, and said she was excited about what they could achieve together.
